title: Manyougana
content:
万葉仮名 (Manyōgana)

Definition

Manyōgana (万葉仮名) is an early Japanese writing system in which Chinese characters (kanji) were used purelyfor their phonetic value. Instead of representing meaning, these characters were selected to approximate thesounds of the Japanese language.

This system played a crucial role in the development of the Japanese writing system. Over time, repeatedphonetic usage of kanji led to the creation of two simplified syllabaries:hiragana and katakana.

Hiragana evolved from the cursive (草書, sōsho) forms of entire kanji, resulting in smooth and roundedcharacters. In contrast, katakana originated from selected components of kanji, giving them a more angularand structured appearance.

Katakana Origins

Katakana characters were derived by extracting parts of kanji used in Manyōgana. This process created a morecompact and geometric writing system, primarily used today for foreign words, emphasis, and technical terms.

Important Notes

In Manyōgana, a single syllable could be represented by multiple kanji. For example, the sound "ka" could bewritten using 加, 可, 香, and many others.

Modern kana systems are standardized forms that emerged from these variations, making reading and writingsignificantly more efficient.

Understanding Manyōgana provides valuable insight into the historical evolution of the Japanese writingsystem and helps learners better appreciate the structure of kana.
